requirements.text: Core must remain technology-neutral; adding a new software technology must not require technology-name branches in generic core lifecycle logic.
New project creation must be neutral; Planner defines repository architecture from requirements rather than a language/project-type generator.
Every project must use a Planner-owned ProjectBlueprint separate from the Plan, with stable requirement/component/interface/verification identities and end-to-end requirements traceability.

Provider must be a thin modular technology contract defining capabilities, compatibility, environment requirements, acceptance, permissions, actions, and normalized outcomes rather than a second lifecycle engine.
Provider/test environments must be framework-managed projects supporting compatible environment families and immutable verified generations.
Material deployment/test/runtime target decisions are user-authoritative; Planner may choose only when delegated and must document the exact choice/rationale.

Provider/Tester/Coder feasibility failures must route to targeted Planner replanning without downstream improvisation; a Planner replan after human approval requires a revised approval package and human reapproval.
Provider/environment failure must remain distinct from candidate/project failure and must not create false evidence against the candidate.
Core/bootstrap must remain small, acyclic, and depend on generic environment build/run primitives rather than a technology-specific provider or permanent Docker-specific contract.
Framework-created projects that remain in service must have an explicit compatibility/migration path; historical work-item data may use a deterministic conversion tool.
User semantic edits to an approval package/project knowledge must create a new unapproved revision and rerun affected validation/feasibility before approval.

The framework repository itself must be developed and updated through the same ProjectBlueprint, traceability, feasibility, approval, candidate, verification, and promotion discipline, with an independent recovery boundary.

Providers originate only from framework/user-managed provider projects; no external provider catalog/store is trusted. A locally promoted provider may be installed/activated automatically for an approved capability requirement, while creating a missing provider requires human-approved architectural work.
Required verification must run through the approved Blueprint-bound provider/environment capability; incidental tools in the framework control plane may provide advisory self-tests only.

Shared environment generations are immutable and space-aware: project dependencies execute in approved isolated overlays, heavy artifacts are garbage-collected by policy, and durable generation/evidence identity survives artifact eviction.

Project/provider execution must use the generic environment backend with immutable/read-only candidate input and isolated writable outputs; provider/domain code must not bypass it to gain undeclared host/container privileges.

Role behavior must be enforced by role-specific context/permission/output/workflow contracts, and Tester-to-Coder handoff must expose all approved requirements while retaining a meaningful independent verification subset (approximately 30% of concrete test information by default) outside Coder context.

Artifact validity/traceability must use an explicit typed dependency DAG with targeted stale propagation and immutable historical revisions/evidence; Project Baselines/savepoints must bound the normal active working graph without deleting traceability.

The framework must make dependency state understandable and scalable through static graph/subgraph visualization in v2.1, future-compatible canonical graph APIs, and measured performance/storage behavior across large synthetic graphs and archived history.

Tester owns development-facing regression tests materialized into the product repository and independent tests stored in framework-managed project knowledge; unilateral Coder test changes are blocked, and provider/environment acceptance tests remain separate.

Every promotion requires a project-defined Final Acceptance Suite drawn from existing VER-* obligations, executed for the exact candidate SHA and required environment generations after prerequisite verification and review.
Debugger is an on-demand read-only diagnosis role for ambiguous, conflicting, or repeated failures; clear ownership routes directly and a diagnosis grants no approval authority.

components.text: Maintain requirements, ProjectBlueprint revisions, stable IDs, design artifacts, and project-level authoritative knowledge.
Produce/revise Blueprint and Plan, reconcile feasibility findings with requirements, and prepare approval-ready engineering change packages.
Maintain requirement -> design -> implementation -> verification -> evidence links and validate trace completeness.
Discover/resolve locally promoted provider contracts and expose technology capabilities/compatibility without embedding domain control flow in core.
Resolve/reuse/create/update provider environment families, generations, overlays, and environment-project work.
Own lifecycle state, targeted replanning routing, candidate identity, failure ownership, and resume behavior.
Build/version Engineering Change Packages, invalidate stale approval, present semantic diffs, and enforce human gates.
Provide generic environment build/run/mount/evidence primitives independent of provider technology and initially implementable with Docker.
Bind normalized verification/environment evidence to candidate and environment identities and preserve audit history.
Convert supported historical work-item/project metadata and preserve/report provenance without inventing ambiguous data.
Apply the framework lifecycle to the framework repository while preserving stable-controller/recovery separation.
Maintain typed artifact dependencies, validity state, baseline/savepoint frontiers, historical archive references, graph queries, compaction, and explanatory graph projections.

interfaces.text: Canonical ProjectBlueprint schema plus stable identity/lineage/traceability semantics.
Revisioned Engineering Change Package joining requirements, Blueprint, Plan, feasibility, scope, verification and risk/permission facts.
Generic build/run/input-mount/output/evidence/artifact identity interface used by environment projects/providers.
Role-specific feasibility/artifact/verdict/diagnostic contracts; must not force incompatible roles into one generic pass/fail semantic.
Canonical typed graph/query/action contract used by lifecycle logic, CLI/static rendering, and future VS Code visualization/control surfaces.

verification_obligations.text: Synthetic unknown provider works end-to-end without adding its technology name/special-case branch to generic core.
Small project preserves complete `REQ-* -> CMP/IFACE -> implementation -> VER-* -> evidence` traceability.
Multi-component project supports targeted replan/invalidation while preserving unaffected traceable artifacts.
User edit of an approval package makes it unapproved, reruns affected feasibility, preserves managed IDs/lineage, and requires explicit final approval.
Post-approval Coder/Tester/Provider finding that causes Planner replan produces a new approval package revision and blocks implementation until human reapproval.
Missing provider environment can be created as a framework-managed environment project from lower-level bootstrap capabilities and then used for project verification.
Incompatible environment variants coexist as separate families; compatible projects reuse promoted generations without in-place mutation.

Controlled environment failure is classified as environment failure, preserves the application candidate, repairs via environment-project lifecycle, and re-verifies the same candidate where source is unchanged.
Core QA passes with optional technology providers absent and detects reintroduced domain-specific core hardcoding.
Framework self-change follows its own requirements/Blueprint/feasibility/approval/implementation/evidence flow while the accepted framework remains recoverable.
Framework architecture release is rejected when current ProjectBlueprint/traceability and implemented architecture materially disagree.
Supported older framework-created project can be maintained/migrated without requiring obsolete project-type classification.

Project requiring a locally promoted provider automatically activates/installs it and creates/reuses its environment without external provider retrieval; a genuinely missing provider blocks on an approved provider-project change.
Required verification cannot be satisfied by an incidental compatible tool in `main-development`; the bound provider/environment execution and exact environment generation are recorded in evidence.

Disk-pressure cleanup removes overlays/caches/eligible heavy environment artifacts in policy order while preserving promoted active environment integrity and durable generation/provenance/evidence records.
Authoritative verification cannot modify the candidate worktree; writes occur only in isolated backend-managed state and undeclared direct privileged backend escape is rejected/detected.

Role-enforcement acceptance proves Coder cannot access retained independent test artifacts through normal role context, receives all approval-bound acceptance requirements, cannot satisfy a Tester verdict with a Coder artifact, and independent tests remain traceable to existing `VER-*` obligations without introducing hidden requirements.

Targeted invalidation acceptance proves an upstream change stales only declared descendants, preserves unaffected current artifacts, explains the dependency path, and creates/restores a Project Baseline whose compaction/archive preserves historical traceability.

Graph scalability/visualization acceptance exercises approximately 1k/10k/100k-node synthetic graphs plus large archived history, measures traversal/stale/cycle/baseline/archive/render/memory/storage behavior, and verifies static focused views are produced from the canonical graph without requiring all nodes to be rendered at once.
Verify Tester-owned repository test materialization, blocked Coder edits, isolation of independent test source and logs, and separate provider/environment acceptance storage.
Reject promotion with missing, failed, stale, wrong-candidate, wrong-suite, wrong-environment, or incomplete required-matrix Final Acceptance evidence; permit only exact current passing bindings.
Route clear candidate/test/environment/architecture failures directly; invoke Debugger for ambiguous/conflicting/repeated failures; reject diagnosis as a verification or approval artifact.
